Infrastructure/Morgan's-Obsidian-Guide.title: Morgan's Obsidian Guide
Infrastructure/Morgan's-Obsidian-Guide.content:
Using Obsidian
Obsidian is a Swiss army knife.
At its core, it is a markdown editor which renders in real time. This makes it fantastic for keyboard users, because there’s no menu to click to create a list or checkbox or do text formatting, you simply type and it appears :)
Files created in Obsidian are not proprietary. You can open them in any text editor. You can also use Obsidian to view markdown or plain text files created elsewhere. This is nice because it means if you grow tired of the app, or you find something better, you can move with low friction.
It is widely extensible. It can become an “everything app”, but you get to decide how big it gets.

NOTE: I recommend growing Obsidian’s functions as you need them rather than in anticipation of your needs. It can very quickly become overwhelming. Start with theming/UI, make it a comfortable place to “be” and then start driving.

Obsidian has “core” functions, which are shipped with the app. It also has community plugins which can be installed piecewise at a user’s discretion. Some plugins are dependant on other plugins. To install a plugin, search for it in Obsidian settings after turning off restricted mode.
Things I do

Daily notes + task management
Documentation / reference creation

This includes work stuff, but also things like recipes, meal plans, blog posts, running gift lists for friends etc.


Publishing
Quick file viewing (pasted images, pdf files, epubs etc.) - see Awesome Reader
Obsidian on mobile

Things I don’t do, despite Obsidian capabilities

Calendar event management
Extensive data work

This may be changing soon :) Obsidian just introduced Bases (databases, excel-like sheets) and I haven’t had a chance to play with them, but they look like a huge improvement over previous table hacks.


Mind maps / network visualisations

Features & Functionality
Templates
See Obsidian Help Docs - Templates.
Templates let you add pre-formatted text to your notes. You can do this for an entire note, or just a snippet (ex. a “preamble” or a formatted checklist).
I have two main templates: my daily work note and my daily non-work note. Command + T on mac lets you pick a template to insert.
These are glorified to-do lists, with space to jot down other thoughts or notes that happen that day. You can use plug-in features with notes. You can also set a default template for all notes, or a template for just “daily” notes. Templates have variables like {{date}} that let you adapt them to the context they live in.
In addition to templates, I have a keyboard shortcut via hammerspoon that types out the current date (YYYY-MM-DD). I use this to quickly label notes/sections. You can get similar functionality with Text Expander or by making an obsidian template that is simply {{date}} :)
Theming and Appearance
I use Minimal Theme to create a “reduced distraction” interface.
I also have various parts of the application hidden. You can customise these settings in Obsidian Settings > Appearance.
If you’re on Windows, you may find the Hider plugin helpful to hide things beyond what Obsidian enables by default.
Outline

Outline
Like the google docs view of headings/table of contents, this enables you to view the document outline of your currently open file.

Hotkeys

Hotkeys
Obsidian lets you assign hotkeys to nearly every action, including those furnished by community plugins. You can add or adjust the native hotkey commands in settings.

Calendar

Calendar

If you plan to use Obsidian for daily/weekly/etc tracking, this is a huge help. It creates a calendar view where notes can be accessed by clicking on weeks, days, or months. I use the daily notes, well, daily, and populate them with my templates from above.
You can also see at a glance which days have incomplete tasks in their notes (hollow dot) or what your word count for a particular day is (number of dots). All of this is customizable.
Tasks

Tasks

You can create tasks with deadlines, tasks that recur, mark tasks as done or cancelled etc.
Some of this is overkill for me; I mostly create basic lists and then “forward” tasks between days bullet-journal style. However, it is much more lightweight than using something like Todoist or Apple Reminders so I still rely on it for ex. self reflection deadlines.
Publishing
Gist support

Share as Gist

I share a lot of code examples / quick thoughts, and I don’t always want to publish to my personal website. For this, I use github gists. Publications can be public or private, and markdown is rendered as you see it in Obsidian (minus any plugin quirks). Subsequent “publish” actions are rendered as updates to the same page, so your URL doesn’t change.
Here is an example of a gist published from Obsidian. We can look at it together and compare it to the note I created locally and rendered on Quartz: Mozilla Git Workflow Notes (FYI: To link to an Obsidian note, you’ll type [[ and then search for the note name)
Quartz

Quartz
Quartz lets you turn your markdown files into a simple website. In fact, the Quartz website is built on Quartz :)
Obsidian integrates very easily with Quartz, and you can choose to publish your entire vault or a smaller set of files.
It essentially enables you to blog directly from Obsidian.app, though Quartz affectionately refers to its publications as digital gardens, a worthwhile distinction which aligns with the way I think of and use Obsidian.
You can also read my guide on Private publishing with Quartz, Obsidian, and Github Pages

Vault “Sync” / Backup


I back up my vault to both iCloud Drive and Github (in a private repository). I do not use the obsidian sync service, though I have heard good things.

Why both?

iCloud Drive means I can access my notes on my phone, iPad, and other computers that sync to my iCloud account. This is for ease, not necessarily part of a 3 - 2 - 1 strategy.
Github is my main backup. I like having all the versions of my past notes, and it protects me in the case of accidental deletion.

I have a local copy of the github repository on my Synology, where I can’t run Obsidian directly but I can edit notes + push them ⇒ see them reflected in Obsidian on my Obsidian-supported devices.







To set up the iCloud backup, I chose a folder inside my iCloud drive during initial vault creation. I ran into problems with this for a bit (various files not loading, styles being wrong) until I right-clicked on the obsidian vault folder and selected “Keep Downloaded”.





My github backup (github.com/MReschenberg/obsidian) is managed by a cron job on my computer. This script file (git_push.sh, below) is saved in the same directory as my obsidian vault. I ran crontab -e and pasted in this formatted line to get it to run every dat at 2AM. It adds all changes and commits them. I have github SSH keys set up on my computer, so this happens without needing to auth.

0 2 * * * bash $OBSIDIAN_PATH/git_push.sh



#! /bin/bash
# Date in format Day-Month-Year
date=$(date +"%Y-%m-%d %T")
# Commit message
message="Commit for $date"
git add -A
git commit -m"${message}"
status="$(git status --branch --porcelain)"
echo $status >> ~/cron_echo.txt
if [ "$status" == "## master...origin/master" ]; then
  echo "No changes" >> ~/cron_echo.txt
else
  echo "There is stuff to push" >> ~/cron_echo.txt
  git push
fi

Infrastructure/Private-publishing-with-Q.title: Private publishing with Quartz, Obsidian, and Github Pages
Infrastructure/Private-publishing-with-Q.content:
Outcome
This guide enables you to publish files from Obsidian to the web, without leaving Obsidian. At the end of it, you’ll be able to press one keyboard command and have your files visible at a URL.
Why do I want this?
The default building and publishing instructions for Quartz and Github Pages assume your markdown files are stored within a public Github repository. For those publishing from Obsidian, this may be undesirable — you may have both private and public files in your vault.
The following instructions describe how to publish with Quartz on Github Pages while maintaining your Obsidian vault in a separate, non-public location.

Note: These instructions require you use Obsidian on a machine that can build Quartz. This will not work, for example, from the Obsidian iOS app.

Let’s go!
This workflow hews as close as possible to the original Quartz/Github Pages instructions for maintainability. To start you should follow the Quartz instructions for cloning. You should also set up your own Github repo for your Quartz site.
The rest of these instructions assume your Obsidian content is located at $OBSIDIAN_PATH. This path should be absolute (not relative) and point to the root directory of your vault (this is the folder that contains the .obsidian directory). When this variable is mentioned, substitute it with your value.
If you store your vault in iCloud like me, make sure your path is correctly escaped for special characters like spaces (e.g. .../Mobile Documents/... should be .../Mobile\ Documents/...). The following instructions are intended for a Unix system.
Quartz Customisation
If you would prefer to opt-in to publishing rather than have each file in your Obsidian vault published by default, I recommend enabling the ExplicitPublish plugin filter. You can read more about this plugin on the Quartz site or add it to your configuration by modifying the following line in your quartz.config.ts:
filters: [Plugin.ExplicitPublish()],
This plugin requires you add a file property of publish: true to any file you wish to show on your Quartz site. By default, any .md without this property will not be published. Other file types will still be published, however.
If you wish to exclude entire folders (e.g. your Attachments folder of images) you can utilise the ignorePatterns parameter like so:
ignorePatterns: ["private", "tempaltes", "Attachments",],
While you’re here, you should ensure your base URL is configured in quartz.config.ts:
baseUrl: "GithubUsername.github.io/QuartzRepositoryName",
Building, Serving, and Syncing Quartz
We’ll need to adjust the default build and serve commands we use for Quartz, as they rely on a few assumptions that we will break:

Quartz assumes content served for your site lives in the content directory
Quartz assumes you want your site’s static files written to a directory called public/

Luckily, Quartz is a fantastic piece of software and provides command line arguments for this work.
Building and Serving
To solve the first problem, we’ll use the --directory argument to pass our $OBSIDIAN_PATH. You should do this both when building (standalone) and serving (using --serve).
To solve the second problem, we’ll use the --o flag to change the name of our output directory. You should pass the string “docs” for this value, to support a Github Pages change we’ll make later.
Your final build command should look something like this:
npx quartz build --directory=$OBSIDIAN_PATH --o docs
Your serve command should look quite similar :)
npx quartz build --directory=$OBSIDIAN_PATH --o docs --serve
Syncing
To synchronise your local Quartz directory with your Github repo, you should run npx quartz sync or npx quartz sync --no-pull per the Quartz documentation. No changes are necessary for this command.
Publishing to Github Pages
The Quartz instructions for Github Pages deployment involve configuring a Github Actions script to build and serve your content on a Github server.
We can forgo this and instead instruct Github to publish our already-generated static files directly. To enable this, open your Quartz repo on Github’s website.

Navigate to your repo’s settings
From the lefthand sidebar, select “Pages”
Under “Build and Deployment > Source” select “Deploy from a branch”
Select the main branch of your Quartz repo (mine is currently called “v4”)
In the dropdown next to the branch, modify the selection from / (root) to /docs
Hit “Save” to the right of the directory selector
Wait a few minutes and refresh the page — you should see a banner declaring your site is live!

Your site should now be available for viewing at GithubUsername.github.io/QuartzRepositoryName
Pushing Changes From Obsidian
Now that your site is up and running, you can create an Obsidian command to build and sync without having to open your terminal.
Create Your Shell Script
First, let’s create a shell script within our Quartz repo that lets us run the Quartz build commands we discussed earlier. I’ve called this publish.sh in my local repo.
npx quartz build --directory=$OBSIDIAN_PATH --o docs && npx quartz sync --no-pull
You may wish to add this to your .gitignore, otherwise it will show up in your public repo.
Use Obsidian’s Shell Command Plugin
Open your Obsidian settings and navigate to Community Plugins. If you haven’t disabled “Restricted Mode”, you’ll need to do that first.
Hit “Browse” and search for “Shell commands”. Install the plugin and enable it from the “Installed Plugins” list (you may need to restart Obsidian).
Once the plugin is installed, you should see it in the Obsidian settings sidebar. Open its settings and create a new shell command called “Publish to Quartz” with the following value:
cd $QUARTZ_PATH && ./publish.sh

Note: Similar to $OBSIDIAN_PATH, $QUARTZ_PATH represents the absolute path to the root directory of your local Quartz repo (this is the directory that contains .quartz-cache and /docs). You should substitute $QUARTZ_PATH with your value.

After you’ve created this command, you should be able to search and execute it from your Obsidian command palette.
If you run into trouble with custom shells, see these instructions.
Hotkey Mapping
Because Obsidian is infinitely customisable, you are able to map this command to a hotkey combination. To do so, open Obsidian settings and navigate to “Hotkeys”. Then, search for “Shell command: Publish to Quartz”. Select it, press your desired key combination, and you’re all set!
Enjoy!

Personal/Recipes/Black-Bean-Soup.title: Black Bean Soup
Personal/Recipes/Black-Bean-Soup.content:
Ingredients
Fresh / Canned

 1 pound dried black beans (not soaked)
 1 yellow onion, peeled, trimmed and quartered
 5 garlic cloves, smashed and peeled

Spices

 Dried pepper of your choosing, I do chipotle
 2 teaspoons ground cumin
 2 dried bay leaves and/or 1 teaspoon dried oregano
 ¼ teaspoon baking soda (optional)
 Kosher salt (Diamond Crystal)
 1 teaspoon apple cider vinegar

Serve with

 Any combination of sour cream, Greek yogurt, corn chips, pickled red onion, cilantro, lime wedges or poached eggs

Instructions
Prep

Peel, quarter onion
Peel garlic

Cooking

In instant pot, combine the beans, onion, garlic, chipotle chile, cumin, bay leaves and/or oregano, and baking soda, if using.
Add 6 cups of water and 1 teaspoon salt and stir to combine.
Cover and cook on low until the beans are tender, 8 to 10 hours.

Taste more than one bean to ensure they’re all cooked through; they should also flatten without much effort when pressed between your fingers.



Serving

Remove and compost the bay leaves.
Transfer the onion, garlic and chipotle chile to a blender or food processor, along with about 2 cups of the beans and broth.

You can purée more or less of the soup, depending on desired consistency.


Blend until smooth. Pour puréed soup back into the slow cooker, stir in the vinegar, then season to taste with salt.
Eat with desired toppings.

Personal/Recipes/Crunchy-Salad.title: Crunchy Salad
Personal/Recipes/Crunchy-Salad.content:
Crispy Rice

 4 cups cooked rice
 1 tbsp chili crisp

Bake at 400°F for ~20 min, stirring every 10. It gets really crunchy really fast, so watch out!
Salad

 1 cucumber, seeded
 1 cup diced, roasted sweet potatoes — can cook at the same time as the crispy rice
 1–2 red bell peppers
 1 bag sugar snap peas
 2 cups pre-cooked edamame
 1 bunch cilantro
 1 bunch mint

Chop and toss all together in a big bowl.
Dressing

 ¼ cup tamari or soy sauce
 ¼ cup rice wine vinegar
 2 tbsp sesame oil
 1 tsp sugar
 Juice of 2 limes
 1 tbsp crunchy peanut butter

Shake until smooth.

Personal/Recipes/Focaccia.title: Focaccia
Personal/Recipes/Focaccia.content:
Ingredients

 2 cups of water
 2 tsp yeast
 2 tsp salt
 1 Tbsp oil
 3 1/2 cups of flour

Mix all ingredients, let sit until doubled or overnight. Place in oiled pan, dimple, second rise.
Bake at 450 for 30 min

Personal/Recipes/Open-face-veggie-sando.title: Open-face veggie sando
Personal/Recipes/Open-face-veggie-sando.content:
Herbed Mayo

1/4c Mayo (I like kewpie)
~1/8c Chopped chives
3 tsp Crushed garlic (if you use frozen, microwave it for ~15 seconds)

Sando ingredients

2-3 slices Good sourdough bread
Aged sharp cheddar
3, 1/2in slices of Italian eggplant
1 Brined red pepper sliced into spears
Dijon mustard
Spices for eggplant: smoked paprika, chili powder, black pepper

Instructions

Salt eggplant slices and set aside for 5 minutes
Combine ingredients for herbed mayo and let sit for 5-10 minutes or overnight in the fridge
Heat cast iron over medium
Season eggplant slices and cook in cast iron, approx 2 minutes per side or until golden brown
Spread mayo on one side of bread, dijon mustard on the opposite side. Place bread mayo-side down in cast iron, still over medium heat.
Top bread with cheese, sliced red pepper, and seared eggplant
Cover, reduce heat to low and cook until cheese is melted and bread is crispy

Personal/Recipes/Ratatouille-Mac--and--C.title: Ratatouille Mac & Cheese
Personal/Recipes/Ratatouille-Mac--and--C.content:
Ingredients
Mac & Cheese

 1 cup gruyere blend cheese, shredded
 1/2 cup cheddar cheese, shredded
 1 tbsp butter
 3 shallot bulbs
 3-4 cloves garlic, chopped
 1/2 tsp paprika
 3/4c cream
 3/4 lbs macaroni pasta, cooked
 1/2c pasta water

Ratatouille

 1 can diced tomatoes
 1/2 eggplant, diced
 1-2 zucchini, sliced
 1 red onion, chopped/diced
 3-4 cloves of garlic, chopped
 2 tsp umami seasoning (TJ’s)
 Olive oil

Instructions

Preheat oven to 400°F
On 1/2 size baking sheet, or two 1/4 size baking sheets, spread zucchini, eggplant, tomatoes, onion, garlic. Drizzle olive oil to taste and mix. Add umami seasoning.
Cook for 20 minutes, stir, cook 15 minutes
In a wide sauce pan, melt butter. Add shallots and garlic. Cook until browned/carmalised. Add paprika.
Cook pasta to package directions, drain and reserve 1/2 cup pasta water.
Add cooked pasta to sauce pan, toss with onions, garlic.
Stir in cheese, cream. Cover, cook on low for a few minutes
If mac is too thick, add in pasta water or more cream
Top with ground black pepper, salt if desired.

To serve: top mac and cheese with ratatouille when plated.

Personal/Recipes/Southwest-Soup.title: Southwest Soup
Personal/Recipes/Southwest-Soup.content:
Adapted from: peasandcrayons.com/2017/02/vegetarian-lentil-tortilla-soup.html
Ingredients
Fresh / Canned

 1 can pinto beans
 1 can black beans
 1 can corn
 1 can tomatoes (any kind)
 1 jar salsa (any kind, usually TJ’s pepito salsa)
 1.5c red lentils
 1 onion (yellow or red), chopped
 6 cloves garlic

Spices

 3-6 bay leaves
 Paprika (smoked or regular)
 Cumin powder
 Cayenne pepper
 Salt and pepper to taste
 3 veggie bullion cubes, chopped

Serve with

 Tortilla chips
 Sour cream
 Mexican cheese

Instructions
Prep

Combine all Fresh/Canned Ingredients and Spices in a large mixing bowl. Mix thoroughly.
Divide mixture into 3-4 quart sized freezer ziplock bags or 1 gallon bag if using larger (family sized) crockpot
Freeze flat

Cooking

Dump frozen mixture into crockpot
Add water to cover (in small crockpot, usually ~3 cups)
Set crockpot to low for about five hours or high for about three hours
Blend thoroughly with immersion blender

Serving

Serve over tortilla chips, top with mexican cheese and sour cream

Work/Documentation/Mozilla-Git-Workflow-.title: Mozilla Git Workflow Notes
Work/Documentation/Mozilla-Git-Workflow-.content:
General Advice / Differences

You’ll want to create a git branch to store work before beginning the work itself. This can be done with git checkout -b YOUR_BRANCH_NAME. You can view branches with git branch -v and switch between them with git checkout BRANCH_NAME. Git’s main branch points to the tip of mozilla-central from the last time you pulled.
Git requires you stage commands to tracked files before they are included in your current commit. Mercurial only requires this for additions and deletions.

You can stage changes for tracked files quickly with git add -u but this will not include any new files. It will include deletions.
git add . by contrast will include new files and modifications but not deletions.
git add -A will include all changes.


It is recommended to install git revise for more efficient building (since git rebase touches files, not just diffs). This is especially recommended on windows where build times are already slow. On mac, you can install this with brew install git-revise. Find more info here

Command Conversions

































































Command DescriptionHG CommandGit CommandUpdate your current working directory to your locally available copy of mozilla centralhg up centralgit checkout mainFetch the latest set of changes for mozilla centralhg up central && hg pull -u centralgit checkout main && git pull origin mainThrow away changes in your working directory, revert to the most recent top commithg up tip --cleangit reset --hard HEADRemove commits from your tree starting at the tip / most recent commitrun hg pune -r tip as many times as necessary lolgit branch -D BRANCH_NAME if all work is on one branch (and you are not on that branch)git reset --soft HEAD~4 where 4 is number of commits in your stack (exclusive). This will leave your working directory untouched.Take changes from your working directory and bundle them into your most recent commithg commit --amend or hg absorbgit commit --amendEdit commit history (ex. squash commits together, take changes in your working directory and parcel them out to older commits)hg histeditgit rebase -i HEAD~4 will let you mess with the 3 most recent commits, for ex.git revise -i will do the same thing :)Commit only certain chunkshg commit -igit commit -iView all in-progress bugs and their patcheshg wipgit log --branches --remotes=origin --not --remotes=upstream --simplify-by-decoration --decorate --oneline --graph --format=format:'%C(green)%h %C(ul magenta)%aL%C(reset) %C(auto)%d%C(reset) %s %C(dim)%ar' git log --graph --oneline --branches --not --remotes --format=format:'%C(green)%h %C(ul magenta)%aL%C(reset) %C(auto)%d%C(reset) %s %C(dim)%ar'you can add a .git/config [alias] section to set wip = one of the commands above then git wip will do this :)Rebase patch stacks on central after updating centralhg rebase -s BASE_REV -d centralgit rebase main BRANCH_NAME NOTE SOURCE AND DEST ARE SWAPPEDif you are already checked out to BRANCH_NAME, you can simply run git rebase mainView changes you’ve made since last committinghg diffgit diff if changes have not been stagedgit diff HEAD^! if they have been stagedView commit you’re currently onhg parentgit log -l 1
Commit Hooks
Lint files before committing
#!/bin/sh

FILES=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR | sed 's| |\\ |g')
[ -z "$FILES" ] && exit 0

# Lint all selected files
echo "$FILES" | xargs ./mach lint --fix

# Add back the modified/linted files to staging
echo "$FILES" | xargs git add

exit 0

Work/Documentation/bug-verification-work.title: bug-verification-worked-examples
Work/Documentation/bug-verification-work.content:
Bug Verification — Worked Examples
Each example below traces a real, recently closed bug through the flowchart in bug-verification-flowchart. For every decision point, the example states: what was found, why that finding leads to the next step (or to a stop), and why the alternative branch was not taken.
All six examples below resolve as generic bugs — stopping at Step 1 or at Focus Management Testing. This is the most common outcome for bugs surfaced through Fable tests and AT audits: the fix is in the markup, and once you see the problem in the core tree, there is no reason to continue.

Example 1 — Multiple unlabeled inputs
Bug: 2041441 · Settings UI · S2
Category: Missing accessible name — label not programmatically associated
flowchart LR
    PRE["🔍 Before you open any tool"] --> REF["📋 Bug symptom reference"]
    REF --> S1["Step 1: Check core a11y tree"]
    S1 --> STOP1(["✅ STOP: File as generic (Desktop)"])
    STOP1 --> FIL["📝 Filing"]
    style PRE fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f
    style REF fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,color:#3b0764
    style S1 fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f
    style STOP1 fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#14532d
    style FIL fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f

Before you open any tool
Q1 — What did the user report?
Several form inputs in about:preferences (Sync, Home, Privacy pages) are announced by screen readers without any name — just the role and type. For example, a text field in the Connection Settings dialog is announced as “edit text” with no indication of what it is for.
Q2 — AT and OS?
Screen readers on multiple platforms.
Q3 — Focus management bug?
No. The user is reporting what the AT announces about specific elements — a naming issue, not a focus movement issue. Stay on the tree path.
Q4 — Hypothesis:
If this is a generic bug, the name field in the core a11y tree will be empty for these inputs. Adjacent visible text is not wrapped in a <label for=""> element, so no name is computed.

Step 1: Check the core a11y tree
Self-check answer: I am looking for the name field on each affected input. If it is empty, the bug is in the markup and affects all ATs.
What I found: The name field is empty for each affected input. The adjacent text that serves as a visual label has no programmatic association to the input.
Decision: absent → file as generic. Stop here.
Why stop: A name that does not exist in the core tree cannot exist in any platform tree. No AT on any platform will ever announce a label for these inputs, because there is nothing for any platform tree to pick up. The fix — adding <label for=""> or aria-labelledby — changes what the core tree computes, which then propagates everywhere.
Why not Step 2: Testing a second AT would only confirm that it also fails to announce a label. It cannot tell us anything new about why the label is missing. We already know why: the name is absent from the core tree.

Filing
Scope: Desktop, no OS, no AT.
Severity: S2 (significant — affects core form usability for screen reader users).
access keyword: required (Settings UI is not a Disability Access module).

Example 2 — Non-descriptive button names
Bug: 2008119 · New Tab Page · S3
Category: Name present but non-descriptive — context missing from computed label
flowchart LR
    PRE["🔍 Before you open any tool"] --> REF["📋 Bug symptom reference"]
    REF --> S1["Step 1: Check core a11y tree"]
    S1 --> STOP1(["✅ STOP: File as generic (Desktop)"])
    STOP1 --> FIL["📝 Filing"]
    style PRE fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f
    style REF fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,color:#3b0764
    style S1 fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f
    style STOP1 fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#14532d
    style FIL fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f

Before you open any tool
Q1 — What did the user report?
In the Topics dialog (New Tab → Personalize → Topics), multiple buttons are announced identically — “Following,” “Following,” “Following” — with no indication of which topic each one acts on. Users cannot distinguish between them.
Q2 — AT and OS?
Screen reader users, multiple platforms implied.
Q3 — Focus management bug?
No. The user is describing what the AT announces about each button — a naming problem, not a focus movement problem.
Q4 — Hypothesis:
If this is a generic bug, the name field in the core tree will show a value (the button is not unlabeled), but the value will be only “Following” — it will not include the topic name it acts on. The label exists but lacks context.

Step 1: Check the core a11y tree
Self-check answer: I am looking at the name field. I expect it to be non-empty, but I need to check whether the value is sufficient — does it include the topic (“Following Movies,” “Following Sports”) or is it just “Following”?
What I found: name is present and reads “Following.” The button is not unlabeled — it has a name. But the name does not include the topic it acts on, making it identical to every other button in the list.
Decision: present but incorrect value → file as generic. Stop here.
Why stop: The incorrect name is what the core tree computes. Every AT on every platform will read “Following” from the same tree. The fix — adding aria-label="unfollow movies" with topic context — changes the computed name in the core tree. That change applies everywhere.
Why not Step 2: This is different from Example 1 in an important way: the name field is not empty, so you might be tempted to conclude the core tree is fine and test a second AT. But “present” does not mean “correct.” A name that lacks necessary context is a defect in the core tree, and testing a second AT would not change that — it would also read “Following.” The issue is in the markup, not the AT.
Note on this bug type: This is the subtlest case in the table. If you inspect the tree and see a non-empty name, pause and ask: is this name actually correct? Does it give a user enough information to act? If not, you are still looking at a generic bug.

Filing
Scope: Desktop, no OS, no AT.
Severity: S3 (moderate — users can reach the buttons but cannot distinguish them).
access keyword: required.

Example 3 — Missing expanded/collapsed state
Bug: 2008197 · New Tab Page · S3
Category: Missing state attribute — aria-expanded not defined
flowchart LR
    PRE["🔍 Before you open any tool"] --> REF["📋 Bug symptom reference"]
    REF --> S1["Step 1: Check core a11y tree"]
    S1 --> STOP1(["✅ STOP: File as generic (Desktop)"])
    STOP1 --> FIL["📝 Filing"]
    style PRE fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f
    style REF fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,color:#3b0764
    style S1 fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f
    style STOP1 fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#14532d
    style FIL fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f

Before you open any tool
Q1 — What did the user report?
When navigating to the Customize button on the new tab page, the screen reader does not announce whether the panel is expanded or collapsed. The user cannot tell whether their previous keypress opened the panel.
Q2 — AT and OS?
Screen reader, platform not yet determined.
Q3 — Focus management bug?
No. The user is describing missing state information from what the AT announces about the button. Focus is not lost; the announcement is incomplete.
Q4 — Hypothesis:
If this is a generic bug, I will find no aria-expanded state on the button node in the core tree. A state that does not exist in the core tree cannot be reported by any AT.

Step 1: Check the core a11y tree
Self-check answer: I am looking at the states/properties section for the Customize button node. Specifically, I expect aria-expanded to be absent entirely if this is a generic bug.
What I found: The button node is present in the tree and correctly named. The states section does not include aria-expanded — the attribute is simply not there.
Decision: state absent → file as generic. Stop here.
Why stop: A state that does not exist in the core tree does not exist in any platform tree. No AT can report “expanded” or “collapsed” because neither value has been exposed anywhere in the tree. The fix — adding aria-expanded to the button element — adds the state to the core tree, and all platform trees and ATs will then have access to it.
Why not Step 2: There is nothing to test with a second AT. The information the AT would need to report the state simply does not exist yet. Testing VoiceOver after NVDA would give you the same result: silence on the state, because the state is not in the tree for either of them to read.

Filing
Scope: Desktop, no OS, no AT.
Severity: S3 (moderate — users cannot confirm whether their action had the intended effect).
access keyword: required.

Example 4 — Selection state and role both absent
Bug: 2036737 · IP Protection
Category: Missing value and role — aria-checked and radio group semantics not exposed
flowchart LR
    PRE["🔍 Before you open any tool"] --> REF["📋 Bug symptom reference"]
    REF --> S1["Step 1: Check core a11y tree"]
    S1 --> STOP1(["✅ STOP: File as generic (Desktop)"])
    STOP1 --> FIL["📝 Filing"]
    style PRE fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f
    style REF fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,color:#3b0764
    style S1 fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f
    style STOP1 fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#14532d
    style FIL fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f

Before you open any tool
Q1 — What did the user report?
In the VPN location picker, users can navigate the location list but cannot tell which location is currently selected. Screen readers on Windows do not announce “selected,” and on macOS and Linux, no state information is announced at all when navigating or activating a location.
Q2 — AT and OS?
Multiple ATs and OSes. The variation in symptoms across platforms (Windows partial, macOS/Linux none) is notable — but note: the correct response is not to start testing each platform in turn. First check the core tree.
Q3 — Focus management bug?
No. The user can navigate the list; they just cannot tell which item is selected. This is a state and value announcement issue.
Q4 — Hypothesis:
If this is a generic bug, the location items in the core tree will either: (a) have no role that conveys selection semantics (e.g. they are plain listitem nodes without radio or option roles), or (b) have no aria-checked or aria-selected property. The cross-platform variation in symptoms is a clue that the core tree is missing both the role and the value — different platforms and ATs may partially fill in gaps differently, which is why behavior varies.

Step 1: Check the core a11y tree
Self-check answer: I am looking at two things for each location item: the role and any value/state property (aria-checked, aria-selected). I expect both to be absent if this is a generic bug.
What I found: Location items are exposed as generic nodes without a role that conveys selection (no radio, no option). No aria-checked or aria-selected property appears. The core tree has no mechanism to communicate selection state.
Decision: role and value both absent → file as generic. Stop here.
Why stop: The cross-platform variation in symptoms might look like evidence of a platform-specific bug, but it is actually evidence of a generic one: different ATs and platforms handle missing semantics differently (some guess, some stay silent, some partially announce), which is why you get different failure modes on different systems. The root cause — no role, no value in the core tree — is the same everywhere. The fix (adding role="radio" and aria-checked to each item, and wrapping in a radio group) is a markup change that benefits all platforms at once.
Why not Step 2: Testing a second AT would confirm that it also fails to announce selection state. But we already know why — neither the role nor the value is in the core tree. A second AT test would be redundant and would not change the scope or the fix.
Why not interpret the cross-platform variation as a platform-specific signal: The fact that Windows announces partial information and macOS announces nothing does not mean this is a Windows-specific or macOS-specific bug. It means these platforms handle absent semantics differently. The consistent underlying problem is the absence of role and value in the core tree.

Filing
Scope: Desktop, no OS, no AT.
access keyword: required.

Example 5 — Focus lost after button activation
Bug: 2027931 · IP Protection · S3
Category: Focus management — focus lost after activating a toggle
flowchart LR
    PRE["🔍 Before you open any tool"] --> FM["🎯 Focus Management Testing"]
    FM --> STOP1(["✅ STOP: File as generic (Desktop)"])
    STOP1 --> FIL["📝 Filing"]
    style PRE fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f
    style FM fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706,color:#451a03
    style STOP1 fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#14532d
    style FIL fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f

Before you open any tool
Q1 — What did the user report?
After pressing Enter on “Turn off VPN,” the VPN state changes but focus disappears entirely. Pressing Tab afterward takes the user nowhere.
Q2 — AT and OS?
Keyboard navigation with screen reader (the focus loss was observed during keyboard testing).
Q3 — Focus management bug?
Yes. The user pressed a button and focus was subsequently lost. This is a focus management bug. Skip the a11y tree inspection entirely. Go to Focus Management Testing.
Why skip the tree: The a11y tree describes properties of nodes — names, roles, states. It does not describe where focus lands when a button fires an event. No amount of inspecting the tree for this bug will tell us why focus disappears after activation.

Focus Management Testing
Self-check answer: The triggering action is pressing Enter on “Turn off VPN.” Expected behavior: since this is a toggle button, focus should remain on the button after activation (the button still exists — it becomes “Turn on VPN”). Focus moving away or disappearing is the bug.
Step A — Reproduce with keyboard only (no AT):
Activate “Turn off VPN” with Enter. Press Tab. Focus is lost — Tab goes nowhere.
What this means: The focus loss reproduces with keyboard only, without any AT active. This is a code-level bug. It is not caused by the AT’s focus handling — it is caused by how the component manages focus when the button fires. All keyboard users, including all screen reader users on all platforms, are affected.
Decision: reproduces keyboard-only → file as generic. Stop here.
Why stop: A focus management bug that reproduces with keyboard only is definitionally not AT-specific or platform-specific. The fix (keeping focus on the toggle button after state change) is in the JavaScript event handling. That fix will benefit all users equally.
Why not open the a11y tree: The tree would show the button node with correct name, role, and state. Everything looks fine in the tree — because the issue is not with what the node exposes, but with what happens to focus when it is activated. The tree does not model event-driven focus movement.
Why not go to Step 2: There is no AT-specific behavior to test. The bug already reproduces without any AT. Testing VoiceOver or NVDA would confirm that they also experience focus loss, but that would not tell us anything new about scope or cause.

Filing
Scope: Desktop, no OS, no AT.
Severity: S3 (keyboard users lose their place in the interface; must navigate back from the top).
access keyword: required (IP Protection is not a Disability Access module).

Example 6 — Element accessible when visually hidden
Bug: 2029022 · Address Bar · S3
Category: Element present in tree when it should be hidden — aria-hidden absent
flowchart LR
    PRE["🔍 Before you open any tool"] --> REF["📋 Bug symptom reference"]
    REF --> S1["Step 1: Check core a11y tree"]
    S1 --> STOP1(["✅ STOP: File as generic (Desktop)"])
    STOP1 --> FIL["📝 Filing"]
    style PRE fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f
    style REF fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,color:#3b0764
    style S1 fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f
    style STOP1 fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#14532d
    style FIL fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f

Before you open any tool
Q1 — What did the user report?
When navigating the browser toolbar with VoiceOver, a “Google, pick a search engine, button, popup collapsed” is announced — but this button is not visible on screen. When activated, it opens a dropdown even though it appears hidden.
Q2 — AT and OS?
VoiceOver on macOS. (But note: the diagnosis will determine whether this is macOS-specific.)
Q3 — Focus management bug?
No. The user is reaching a control that announces itself — this is not about where focus goes after an action. It is about a control that should not be reachable being in the tree.
Q4 — Hypothesis:
This is the inverse of the usual inspection question. I am not looking for something absent — I am looking for an unwanted presence. If this is a generic bug, the search mode switcher will appear in the core a11y tree without aria-hidden applied to it or any of its ancestors. Its presence in the tree (without hiding) means every AT on every platform can reach it.

Step 1: Check the core a11y tree
Self-check answer: I am looking for the search mode switcher node. I expect to find it present in the tree when it should not be. I am also checking whether aria-hidden or any equivalent hiding mechanism appears on this node or its ancestors.
What I found: The search mode switcher node is present in the core tree. There is no aria-hidden on it or its ancestors. Visually it is hidden (via CSS), but from the tree’s perspective it is fully accessible.
Decision: element present in tree when it should be hidden → file as generic. Stop here.
Why stop: The absence of aria-hidden is a property of the core tree — it is the same on every platform. Any AT on any OS that queries the core tree (and all of them do) will find this node and expose it. The bug is not a quirk of VoiceOver’s behavior; VoiceOver is correctly reporting what it finds. The fix — adding aria-hidden to the switcher when it is visually hidden — changes what is in the core tree, and all ATs on all platforms benefit.
Why not treat this as a macOS/VoiceOver-specific bug: The reporter used VoiceOver on macOS, but that is only because that is the AT they were testing with. NVDA on Windows would also find and announce this node — it is in the core tree, which all ATs consume. The symptom was discovered on macOS, but the scope is not macOS. This is the most common reason to over-scope a bug: the platform of discovery is not the same as the platform of the bug.
Why not Step 2: The node is in the core tree without aria-hidden. Testing a second AT would confirm that it also reaches the node — but that confirms what we already know. The fix is in the markup.

Filing
Scope: Desktop, no OS, no AT.
Severity: S3 (screen reader users encounter phantom interactive controls with no visual counterpart, which is confusing and unpredictable).
access keyword: required.


Example 7 — Toggle not numbered by Voice Control; VoiceOver reaches it fine
Bug: Recent Activity toggle — Settings Redesign Fable test
Category: AT-specific — Voice Control on macOS cannot locate the node; VoiceOver on macOS can
flowchart LR
    PRE["🔍 Before you open any tool"] --> REF["📋 Bug symptom reference"]
    REF --> S1["Step 1: Check core a11y tree"]
    S1 --> S2["Step 2: Test with secondary AT"]
    S2 --> STOP2(["✅ STOP: File as AT-specific (macOS + Voice Control)"])
    STOP2 --> FIL["📝 Filing"]
    style PRE fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f
    style REF fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,color:#3b0764
    style S1 fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f
    style S2 fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f
    style STOP2 fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#14532d
    style FIL fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f

Before you open any tool
Q1 — What did the user report?
A Fable participant using Voice Control on macOS said “show numbers.” The Recent Activity toggle did not receive a number, but every other toggle above it in the list did. The participant could not activate it by number or name.
Q2 — AT and OS?
Voice Control on macOS.
Q3 — Focus management bug?
No. The user is describing an element that Voice Control cannot locate at all — it doesn’t appear in the numbers overlay. This is about whether the element is present in Voice Control’s tree, not about where focus goes after an action.
Q4 — Hypothesis:
If this is a generic bug, the toggle node will be absent from the core tree entirely, which would explain why VC can’t find it. If the node IS in the core tree, the bug is somewhere downstream — in the macOS platform tree or in how Voice Control specifically queries that tree.

Step 1: Check the core a11y tree
Self-check answer: I am looking for the Recent Activity toggle node. If absent → generic. If present with correct name, role, and state → not generic, continue.
What I found:

Node is present.
Name: “Recent activity” ✓
Role: button ✓
State: aria-pressed: true ✓

Everything the AT needs is in the core tree.
Decision: all properties correct → not generic. Continue to Step 2.
Why not stop: If the name, role, and state are all present and correct, the markup is not the problem. The core tree has what Voice Control needs; something further down the stack is failing to surface it.
Why not look further: Checking other properties like aria-describedby or running the automated checker would not tell us why VC can’t number this element. The presence question — is the node in the tree? — is answered. Move on.

Step 2: Test with a secondary AT on the same platform
Self-check answer: VoiceOver is the other major AT on macOS and it also reads the macOS platform tree. If VoiceOver can reach the toggle, the macOS platform tree is intact and the failure is specific to Voice Control. If VoiceOver also cannot reach it, the macOS platform tree itself is broken for this node.
What I found:
Navigate to the Recent Activity toggle with VoiceOver. VoiceOver announces “Recent activity, toggle button.” VoiceOver can reach it and reads both the name and role correctly.
Decision: second AT succeeds → AT-specific. Stop here.
Why stop: VoiceOver and Voice Control both consume the macOS platform tree. VoiceOver can reach this node, which means the macOS platform tree has the information. The failure is specific to how Voice Control queries that tree — Voice Control asks different questions about the platform tree than VoiceOver does, and its particular query is not returning this node. The fix belongs with how Voice Control handles this type of node, not in Firefox’s markup or platform layer.
Why not Step 3: Testing Windows would be redundant. We already know the macOS platform tree is correct (VoiceOver proves this). Filing as macOS + Voice Control is the right scope — there is no reason to believe Windows users are affected.

Filing
Scope: macOS, Voice Control in the bug title.
Severity: S3 (user cannot interact with a control by voice command, but workarounds exist).
access keyword: required.

Example 8 — VPN panel not announced when tabbing with VoiceOver
Bug: 2036874 · Core, Disability Access APIs · macOS
Category: Platform-specific — macOS platform tree represents non-native popovers incorrectly; fix required restructuring how popup windows appear in the macOS accessibility tree
flowchart LR
    PRE["🔍 Before you open any tool"] --> REF["📋 Bug symptom reference"]
    REF --> S1["Step 1: Check core a11y tree"]
    S1 --> S2["Step 2: Test with secondary AT"]
    S2 --> OUT3(["File as platform-specific (macOS · no AT in title)"])
    OUT3 --> FIL["📝 Filing"]
    style PRE fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f
    style REF fill:#ede9fe,stroke:#7c3aed,color:#3b0764
    style S1 fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f
    style S2 fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f
    style OUT3 fill:#fef9c3,stroke:#ca8a04,color:#713f12
    style FIL fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a5f

Before you open any tool
Q1 — What did the user report?
When using VoiceOver on macOS and pressing Tab to navigate through the IP Protection / VPN panel in Firefox, VoiceOver stops announcing the panel content. The panel is reachable with Tab (keyboard focus arrives there), but VoiceOver is silent — it does not read the panel’s heading, buttons, or content.
Q2 — AT and OS?
VoiceOver on macOS.
Q3 — Focus management bug?
No. The user can Tab to the panel — keyboard focus is not lost. The issue is that VoiceOver doesn’t announce what is there. This is an announcement and tree-exposure issue, not a focus management issue.
Q4 — Hypothesis:
If this is a generic bug, the VPN panel node or its contents will be absent from the core tree. If the panel IS in the core tree, the failure is in the macOS platform layer.

Step 1: Check the core a11y tree
Self-check answer: I am looking for the VPN panel node and its content. If absent → generic. If present with correct structure → not generic.
What I found: The VPN panel node is present in the core tree. Its child nodes — headings, toggle buttons, status text — are all present with correct names and roles.
Decision: all properties correct → not generic. Continue to Step 2.
Why not stop: The panel and its contents exist in the core tree. The markup is not the problem. Something in the macOS-specific stack is failing to expose the panel in a way VoiceOver can consume.

Step 2: Test with a secondary AT on the same platform
A note specific to macOS: VoiceOver is the only screen reader on macOS. There is no second screen reader to compare with directly. The secondary AT test on macOS uses Voice Control — not because VC reads out content like a screen reader does, but because VC also queries the macOS platform tree to build its numbers overlay. If VC also cannot interact with the VPN panel’s controls, both ATs are failing to read from the same defective macOS platform tree.
Self-check answer: If Voice Control also fails to number any interactive controls inside the VPN panel, both ATs are reading the same broken platform tree. If Voice Control CAN number them, the problem is specific to how VoiceOver navigates.
What I found: Say “show numbers” over the VPN panel. No numbers appear over the panel’s buttons and toggles. Voice Control also cannot interact with the panel’s content.
Decision: second AT also fails → platform-specific.
Why both failing means platform: VoiceOver and Voice Control both read from the macOS platform tree, but via different APIs. When both fail, the platform tree itself is the problem — not either AT’s specific query logic. The root cause turned out to be that non-native popover windows were being structured as children of the root application node in the macOS platform tree, which neither VoiceOver nor Voice Control could navigate into correctly.
Why not AT-specific: If only VoiceOver failed and Voice Control could still interact with the panel, we would conclude VC’s tree was intact and VO was at fault. But both failing eliminates that explanation.

Step 3 — considered and skipped
We could test on Windows with NVDA to confirm that Windows is unaffected and the bug is macOS-only. However, the root cause — AXPopover windows appearing as children of the root application node — is a macOS-specific accessibility API concept. There is no equivalent structure on Windows or Linux. There is no reason to believe the same structural mistake was made in the Windows platform tree.
Decision: skip Step 3. File as macOS, no AT specified.
Why skip: The technical cause is macOS-specific by nature. We have enough information to file accurately without testing Windows. Testing it would not change the scope of the bug or the fix.

Filing
Scope: macOS, no AT in the bug title.
access keyword: required.

A note on Steps 2 and 3
Examples 1–6 above all resolve at Step 1 or at Focus Management Testing. This is the typical outcome for bugs discovered through Fable tests and AT audits: the failure is in the markup, the core tree reflects it, and there is no need to continue.
Examples 7 and 8 show the less common cases where the core tree is correct. In Example 7, a second AT on the same platform succeeded — confirming the bug is AT-specific and stopping there. In Example 8, both ATs on the same platform failed — confirming the bug is in the macOS platform tree, and Step 3 was skipped because the cause was macOS-specific by design.
The diagnostic question is always the same: does the core tree have what the AT needs? If yes, keep testing downward. If no, stop — the fix belongs in the markup.
